The test image shows a young soybean plant with leaf symptoms: multiple small, dark brown to reddish-brown spots scattered across both leaves, roughly circular to irregular in shape. These appear on the upper leaf surface. The spots look like early-stage leaf lesions. No obvious halos, no angular water-soaked pattern, no white mold, no pustules visible.

Key observations:
- Affected part: leaf
- Small, dark brown/reddish-brown scattered spots on upper leaf surface
- Spots appear circular to irregular
- Young plant, lower canopy leaves affected
- No yellowing halos, not angular/vein-limited

Top candidates:
- **Septoria_brown_spot**: small, irregularly shaped dark brown lesions, both leaf surfaces, lower canopy first — fits well
- **Frogeye_leaf_spot**: circular gray lesions with reddish-brown margins — the spots here appear quite dark/brown without gray centers
- **Bacterial_Blight**: angular, water-soaked — doesn't fit well

The spots are dark brown, scattered, small, irregular — strongly suggesting Septoria_brown_spot. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

This Septoria_brown_spot reference shows small dark brown spots on lower canopy leaves with surrounding yellowing — very similar pattern to the test image. The test image shows the same small, scattered dark brown spots on young soybean leaves, matching the Septoria description: small irregularly shaped dark brown lesions on both leaf surfaces, starting in the lower canopy.

The match is strong: same plant stage, same leaf position, same spot morphology (small, dark brown, scattered, irregular).
